chapter_theme: Tirumular's own story (திருமூலர் வரலாறு): with Nandi's feet on his head he came from Kailasa, saw the dance, served the Goddess, and stayed at Avaduthurai beneath the bodhi tree for ages, in this body. The Lord made him to sing the Lord in Tamil, and he wishes the bliss he gained on the whole world.
structure_note: His resolve to tell the Agama (73, 74); the reasons for his stay, told to Indra and Malangan (75 to 79); his long dwelling and the Lord's purpose in making him (80 to 87); then a run of verses on what Nandi gave him and what he has expounded (88 to 94). Verses 90 and 91 are linked by repeating விளக்கி.

73.reading: Placing Nandi's holy feet on my head, setting them within my mind and praising, thinking daily on the feet of Hara who wears the evening moon, I set out to tell the Agama.
73.nuance: போற்றிசெய் தந்தி is read போற்றிசெய்து அந்தி: the moon of evening. The verse sets the guru's feet before the Lord's, as the preface does throughout.

74.reading: Gaining the feet of gracious Nandi, who grants the teaching that bears the name Siva Agama, and after seeing the matchless dance in the flawless hall, I remained for seven crore ages without equal.
74.nuance: Line 1 may mean that the poet's work gained the name Siva Agama, or that he gained the Agama so named. எழுகோடி யுகம் is a figure of immense time. ஒப்பிலா may go with the ages or with himself.

75.reading: Hear the reason I stayed, Indra: having served the lady of rare austerity, rich in fortune, Bhuvanapati, I came with her out of love and devotion.
75.nuance: Indra is the disciple named in 69. புவனாபதி (lady of the worlds) and அருந்தவச் செல்வி are taken as the Goddess. Whether he came with her or came because of her is not clear.

76.reading: Through Sadasiva, the tattvas, the threefold Tamil and the Veda, I stayed till now keeping a measured diet, and with mind withdrawn and not indifferent, I came to know.
76.nuance: The verse rhymes on Sanskrit forms: மிதாசனி (one who eats sparingly), இதாசனி and உதாசனி (indifferent), which do not yield a firm sense. முத்தமிழ் is Tamil of letters, music and drama. The reading is a guess at the shape of the verse.

77.reading: Malangan, the reason I came here is to tell the Veda of noble limbs of the holy dance, spoken as root and limb with the fine-jewelled one of dark-blue body.
77.nuance: Malangan is the disciple named in 69. மூலாங்கம் and சீலாங்கம் are coined compounds; மூல may pun on Mulan. The 'Veda' he has come to tell is probably his own book.

78.reading: The fine-jewelled one is she whose name is unsurpassed bliss, who cut off my birth and took me as her own; she of glory is at Siva's Avaduthurai, and I reached her feet and stayed.
78.nuance: ஆவடுதண்டுறை is Tiruvavaduturai, where tradition places Tirumular. Here the Goddess, not Nandi or Siva, is the one who ends his births.

79.reading: I stayed joined to the one whose half is Siva's woman; I stayed at Siva's Avaduthurai; I stayed in the shade of Siva's bodhi tree; I stayed reciting Siva's names.
79.nuance: சிவபோதி (Siva's bodhi tree) and நற்போதி in 82 use the word for the Buddha's tree, here for the sacred fig under which the sage sat.

80.reading: I stayed in this body for countless crores; I stayed in the place where there is no night and day; I stayed at the feet the gods praise; I stayed beneath the twin feet of my Nandi.
80.nuance: இராப்பகல் அற்ற இடம் is traditionally a yogic state beyond the alternation of the breaths (read as sun and moon, day and night); plainly it is a place outside time. Staying in this body (இக்காயத்தே) for ages is offered as attainment, not as bondage.

81.reading: Why be born again later? People do not strive at austerity well beforehand. The Lord made me well so that I would render him well in Tamil.
81.nuance: தன்னை நன்றாகத் தமிழ் செய்யுமாறு is usually taken as 'to sing him well in Tamil'. The verse sets others' neglect of tapas against his own purpose. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Kandar Anubhuti 17, where the poet's learning is likewise the Lord's gift.

82.reading: Entering the city of Nandi, consort of the lady of wisdom, I too stayed for nine flawless crore ages beneath the good bodhi tree, worshipping the Lord and bathing him in the milk of wisdom.
82.nuance: ஞானப்பாலாட்டி may be 'bathing in the milk of wisdom' or a title of the Goddess (the nurse who gives wisdom's milk). The ages differ from 74's seven crore, which suggests figures of vastness.

83.reading: A Siva-sage who knows the way to go, a siddha, eminent among sages in conquering wisdom, came by the sky-path that bends toward the many gods, asuras and humans.
83.nuance: சித்தசன் is unclear: a siddha, a name, or Manmatha (சித்தஜன், born of mind) are all possible. Tradition reads the verse of Tirumular's own coming south from Kailasa through the sky.

84.reading: Among the books that excel in the mind, the Father here gave me by grace a body fitting the Veda recited as highest, and the origin that stands within.
84.nuance: ஒத்த உடலையும் (a fitting body too) and உள்நின்ற உற்பத்தி (the origin within) are hard to construe. The plain sense is that the body was given by grace, for the teaching; that fits Tirumular's high view of the body.

85.reading: May this world gain the bliss I gained: if one speaks the hidden meaning that holds the sky, the mantra felt within, that holds to the flesh, comes forward as one holds to it more and more.
85.nuance: The first line is the most quoted in the book and is plain. The rest is not: ஊன்பற்றி நின்ற உணர்வுறு மந்திரம் is traditionally the mantra present in the body as breath or as consciousness, and தலைப்படும் may mean it is attained or that it rises up.

86.reading: The gods go and fold their hands to the unborn Lord, great Nandi; never forgetting him, they can recite the garland of mantras in their hearts, joined to it firmly.
86.nuance: மந்திர மாலை (garland of mantras) is often taken as the Tirumanthiram itself. பிறப்பிலி (the unborn) is a title of Siva given here to Nandi.

87.reading: He set fire within its bounds and set the body, set the seven worlds so they keep within bounds, set the Tamil treatise so it keeps within bounds, and set meaning itself so it does not overflow.
87.nuance: The refrain is மிகாமை (not exceeding) after வைத்தான் (he set). The Lord's ordering of fire, body and worlds is extended to the Tamil sastra and its meaning. எங்குமி and தங்குமி may also divide as இகாமை (not leaving).

88.reading: Brahma and Vishnu, seeking his foot and crown, did not see his form; meeting again on earth, Achyuta said 'I did not see the foot', and Brahma lied, 'I saw the crown'.
88.nuance: The story of Siva as the endless column of fire. Vishnu admits failure and Brahma lies; the verse contrasts their honesty without stating a moral.

89.reading: Our Nandi, the Supreme never parted from bull, deer and axe, gave me release from the moving and unmoving world that is his imagining, and set his good feet on my head.
89.nuance: அற்றம் may be 'end', 'release' or 'secret'. கற்பனை ஆகும் சராசரம் (the world that is his imagining) can be read as the world being his creation or as its being illusory; the verse does not settle which.

90.reading: I have explained in full the known, knowledge and the knower, maya, the supreme power that comes from Mahamaya, the whole assembly, Siva himself, and the seed beyond the senses.
90.nuance: நேயம், ஞானம், ஞாதுரு are the triad of knowable, knowledge and knower. ஆயம் (group, assembly) and அகோசர வீயம் (the imperceptible seed) are technical and unclear. The verse claims the whole Siddhanta scheme for his book.

91.reading: Explaining, I came by the way of boundless Kailasa at the word of the unwavering dancer of bliss, Nandi of bliss and measureless greatness, the light of true wisdom that is the Supreme.
91.nuance: விளக்கி takes up 90's last word. The verse places his coming from Kailasa under the dancer's command, which is how tradition tells his journey south.

92.reading: By Nandi's grace I sought Mulan; then by Nandi's grace I became Sadasiva; by Nandi's grace I entered true wisdom; by Nandi's grace I stayed.
92.nuance: The four lines repeat நந்தி அருளாலே as 68 does. சதாசிவன் ஆயினேன் (I became Sadasiva) is a strong claim of identity with a form of Siva, attributed wholly to the guru's grace.

93.reading: If one stays, countless crores stay there within the consuming root; as sun and moon blaze with fierce fire, the melted hair shines with light.
93.nuance: மூலம் is traditionally the root centre of yoga, and அருக்கன், சோமன் (sun and moon) the two breath channels whose fire is raised. உருக்கிய ரோமம் (melted hair) is obscure; it may describe the yogi's body made radiant. இருக்கு may also pun on the Rig Veda. Both a plain and a yogic reading are uncertain here.

94.reading: Always I babble of great Nandi; I hold him in my heart night and day; I strive toward my Lord of soaring light, who is the Lord, a light shining by its own nature.
94.nuance: பிதற்றுகின்றேன் (I babble) is devotional self-belittling, preparing the chapter on modesty that follows. The last line runs Nandi and the Lord together.

links.note: The Kural says tapas should be striven for here, since it gains what one wishes; Tirumular asks why be born again when people do not strive at tapas beforehand. Both use முயல் and place the effort now.

The Kural's learned love learning more when they see the world delighting in what delights them; Tirumular wishes the bliss he gained on the whole world. Both make a private good complete only when it is shared.
70 has the four masters told 'may you gain all that I gained'; 85 widens the same wish from four disciples to the whole world.

74 says that after seeing the matchless dance in the flawless hall (மன்றில் தனிக்கூத்துக் கண்டபின்) the poet stayed seven crore ages. 132 names what those who worship that dance gain: the great attainment that does not part from that hall (அம்மன்றில் பிரியாப் பெரும்பேறு) and the fruit of not being born. The general promise of 132 is what 74 claims for the poet himself.

75 says the poet served the lady of rare austerity who is Bhuvanapati (புவனாபதியாம் அருந்தவச் செல்வி) and came with her in devotion. 1071, in the chapters on Shakti, praises the red feet of Bhuvanapati (புவனாபதியார்) who turns the deluded mind to the true thing. The title ties the poet's personal history to the Goddess the later tantra teaches.

76 says the poet stayed keeping a measured diet (மிதாசனி யாதிருந்தேன்) until he came to know. 556 counts little food (சுருக்கம்) among the ten rules of niyama. The sense of 76 is uncertain, but read this way the poet's account of himself follows the discipline the book later prescribes.

77 tells Malangan the reason he came: to tell the Veda of the holy dance (திருக்கூத்தின் சீலாங்க வேதத்தைச் செப்ப). 108 gives the commission behind it: the Lord says 'give our feet to the world' (ஞாலத்து நம்மடி நல்கிடு). The pairing shows the book as both the dance's Veda and the giving of the Lord's feet.

78 says the fine-jewelled Goddess cut off his birth and took him as her own (பிறப்பறுத்து ஆண்டவள்). 641 says the Lord, giving great grace, cut off his birth (பிறப்பறுத்தானே) after he saw the pure space. The same verb is given to the Goddess in the preface and to the Lord in the siddhi chapter, so the book does not keep release to one agent.

79 says the poet stayed in the shade of Siva's bodhi tree (சிவபோதியின் நீழலில்) reciting Siva's names; 82 says he stayed beneath the good bodhi tree (நற்போதியின் கீழே) worshipping. Both take the word for the Buddha's tree for the sage's seat, a distinctive borrowing that the two verses share and no other verse of the book uses.

80 says 'I stayed in this body (இக்காயத்தே) for countless crores' as part of his attainment. 725 gives the reason the body is worth keeping: once held a thing of shame, it was found to hold the true substance, the Highest having made it his temple (உடம்புளே உத்தமன் கோயில்கொண்டான்). 725 supplies the doctrine behind 80's claim.

80 offers staying in this body (இருந்தேன் இக்காயத்தே) for countless crores as attainment. Naladiyar 27 praises those who see the body as a bubble in pelting rain that forms and bursts (மொக்குளின் ... கெடும் இதோர் யாக்கை) and resolve to end their wandering. On the literal reading of 80's long bodily stay, the two set opposite values on the body's duration.

84 says the Father gave him by grace a body fitting the Veda (ஒத்த உடலையும் ... அருளால் அளித்ததே). 724 argues why such a body matters: if the body perishes, life perishes and true knowledge cannot be reached, so 'I nurtured the body and nurtured life' (உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன் உயிர்வளர்த்தேனே). The gift in 84 becomes a practice in 724.

86 says the gods, never forgetting Nandi, can recite the garland of mantras in their hearts (மந்திர மாலை ... ஓதலுமாமே). 99 promises that those who recite Mulan's three thousand reach the Lord, but only if they recite knowing the meaning (கருத்தறிந்து ஓதிடின்). 99 adds the condition 86 does not state.

87 says the Lord set fire within bounds (அங்கி மிகாமைவைத்தான்) along with body, worlds and the Tamil sastra. 365, in the chapter on the deluge, uses the same words for the fire he set in the swelling sea so that it would not overflow (அங்கி மிகாமைவைத்தானே). The preface takes the cosmic act of restraint and extends it to the poet's book and its meaning.

89 calls the moving and unmoving world the Supreme's imagining (தற்பரன் கற்பனையாகும் சராசரம்), from which Nandi gave release. 1947 says that when thought is cut off, cause and effect are all imagining (இவை கற்பனை தானே). The shared word கற்பனை shows the book using the same term for the world as the Lord's making and as what dissolves for the freed mind; both verses are uncertain.

90 claims to have explained in full the known, knowledge and the knower (நேயத்தை ஞானத்தை ஞாதுருவத்தினை). 2382 says that in the end the knower subsides in the known (அடங்கிடும் ஞாதுரு) and even the mark of knowledge departs into silence that is Siva's bliss. The triad the preface promises to explain is the triad the late tantra dissolves.

94 says 'always I babble of great Nandi' (பிதற்றுகின்றேன் என்றும் பேர்நந்தி தன்னை), babbling as the devotee's humble speech. 110 says the ignorant babble (பிதற்றுகின்றாரே) as they divide the one light into Isa, Mal and Brahma. The same word marks the poet's praise in one verse and sectarian error in the other.

source_issues: 76: lines 2 to 4 turn on Sanskrit forms (மிதாசனி, இதாசனி, உதாசனி) that do not yield a firm sense; the text may be corrupt.
83: சித்தசன் is unclear (a siddha, a proper name, or Manmatha).
